ProphecySummary: Nahum, whose name means comfort, announced comfort for Judah and doom for Nineveh, the bloody city full of lies and robbery. He pictured chariots raging in the streets, river gates opened, the palace dissolved, and the city plundered of silver and gold without end. The prophet declared there would be no healing of Nineveh's wound, and that all who heard of its fall would clap their hands, for its endless cruelty had touched everyone.
Fulfillment: Nineveh fell in 612 BC after a three-month siege by a coalition of Medes and Babylonians, recorded in the Babylonian Fall of Nineveh Chronicle, and the city was so thoroughly destroyed that it lay as mounds until its rediscovery in the nineteenth century. Nahum's window is secure: he refers to the fall of Thebes in 663 BC as past, and Nineveh was still standing when he wrote, so the fall came within about fifty years of the prophecy. The prophecy is fulfilled.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Nineveh; Fall of Thebes
